content.value_statement: Medical device teams need clear regulatory plans before submission work starts. This skill helps structure pathways, timelines, risks, and stakeholder coordination.
actual_capabilities: Build regulatory pathway plans for FDA, EU MDR, ISO, and global markets.
Outline submission preparation steps and review milestones.
Identify regulatory risks, mitigation actions, and escalation points.
Coordinate cross-functional responsibilities for regulatory programs.
Use the included tracker script to store and report submission status.
limitations: Does not replace legal, clinical, or regulatory authority advice.
Reference material may require updates for current laws and guidance.
Several resources named in SKILL.md are not present in the package.
Tracker data is local and does not integrate with agency systems.

use_cases.title: Define a submission pathway
use_cases.description: Regulatory leads compare FDA 510(k), De Novo, PMA, EU MDR, and ISO options before planning evidence.

use_cases.title: Prepare an approval plan
use_cases.description: Product teams organize documentation, timelines, risk controls, and authority interactions for a medical device launch.

use_cases.title: Monitor active submissions
use_cases.description: Program managers track submission status, overdue items, and approvals using local tracker data.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Pathway Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize likely regulatory pathways for a Class II medical device entering the United States and European Union. Include key evidence needs.

prompt_templates.title: Build Submission Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a practical submission checklist for an FDA 510(k). Include documentation, testing, labeling, quality system, and review milestones.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Regulatory Risk
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this product plan for regulatory risks. Identify likely submission blockers, mitigation actions, owners, and escalation points.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Global Market Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a phased global regulatory strategy for a connected medical device. Compare FDA, EU MDR, ISO, and selected international pathways.

output_examples.input: A team asks which pathway fits a moderate-risk device without a predicate.
output_examples.output: A De Novo strategy summary with evidence gaps, FDA interaction steps, and decision points for market access.

output_examples.input: A product manager needs a 510(k) preparation plan.
output_examples.output: A checklist covering predicate comparison, performance testing, software documentation, labeling, eCopy preparation, and review timelines.

output_examples.input: A program manager wants to know which submissions need attention.
output_examples.output: A status report showing active submissions, overdue target dates, responsible owners, and next regulatory actions.

best_practices: Verify all regulatory assumptions against current agency guidance before use.
Provide product classification, target markets, risk profile, and evidence status in prompts.
Keep tracker data limited to non-sensitive project metadata unless storage controls are approved.
anti_patterns: Treating generated guidance as final legal or regulatory advice.
Using outdated EU MDR or FDA guidance without review.
Storing protected health information in local tracker files.

faq.question: Can this skill make final regulatory decisions?
faq.answer: No. It supports planning and documentation, but qualified regulatory experts must approve final decisions.

faq.question: Does it submit documents to FDA or EU authorities?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and local planning support only.

faq.question: What markets does it cover?
faq.answer: It includes FDA, EU MDR, ISO, and general global regulatory planning references.

faq.question: Can it track submission status?
faq.answer: Yes. The included Python tracker stores local submission records and generates status reports.

faq.question: Does it need internet access?
faq.answer: No evidence found of network calls in the reviewed files.

faq.question: Is it suitable for sensitive data?
faq.answer: Use caution. The tracker writes local files, so sensitive data needs approved storage controls.
